To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the host-country policies have a significant effect on the innovation performance of foreign subsidiaries; (b) this effect is mediated by R&D investment decisions; and (c) the effect of host-country policies on subsidiary innovation performance varies with the subsidiary’s R&D investment decision.

(1) host country technology policies shape the incentives of subsidiaries to invest in R&D, (2) host country technology policy is positively related to subsidiary R&D investment and innovation performance, and (3) the relationship between technology policy and subsidiary R&D investment depends on subsidiary absorptive capacity.
(a) the host country technology policy has a significant impact on subsidiary innovation performance and that (b) this relationship is moderated by the level of subsidiary R&D investments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of host country policies and MNCs’ strategic responses to those policies in shaping subsidiary innovation performance.
the impact of technology policy on the innovative activities of multinational corporations (MNCs), and in particular on the role of MNC subsidiary innovation performance.
the role of the state and public policy in influencing the innovation and technology performance of MNCs.

we have found a strong link between technology policy and the performance of foreign affiliates.
the role of government in innovation and economic growth is a very important one, but it is a very complicated one.

host country technology policy can shape the innovation performance of MNCs.
MNCs’ subsidiary-level R&D investment decisions are influenced by the host country policy regime and that these policy effects are moderated by the subsidiaries’ strategic capabilities.
